A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CORE research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–E are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, compute controls, ablations, five-seed stochastic experiments and qualitative decoding examples.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the stochastic evaluations and qualitative examples in the appendices.

M1.justification: Both versions use margin-based candidate selection, simultaneous masking, instability scoring with one auxiliary forward pass, and greedy revision of selected tokens. Algorithm 1 changes probability notation but retains the same procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate GSM8K, MATH, BBH, HumanEval and MBPP. The reasoning and coding tasks, stochastic evaluations and qualitative example coverage are unchanged.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain Low-Confidence and Top-k Margin unmasking, ReMDM-conf, Random Remask and Margin Remask. The newly discussed related works are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix B retain LLaDA-8B-Base, 128 decoding steps, length 512, the same revision window and settings, evaluation metrics and few-shot counts. The 136-forward-pass controls and sensitivity configurations also match.

E4.justification: Both contain the same selection controls, candidate-size and revision-interval sweeps, instability distributions, stochastic robustness evaluation and qualitative cases. Figures 2–8 and Appendices D–E provide no new analyses.

E5.justification: Both report five stochastic seeds with means and standard deviations in Table 6, two-sided McNemar testing at p < 0.05 in Appendix B, and the same significance markings and fixed-seed compute controls.

E6.justification: Numerical entries in Tables 1–4 and 6 match, as do the plotted results and qualitative example outcomes. For example, both report CORE MBPP accuracy of 24.80 under Low-Confidence greedy decoding and 25.24 ± 0.92 under stochastic decoding.

T1.justification: v3 explicitly introduces token random variables and rewrites Equation (8)'s expectation over masks rather than their induced contexts. These are equivalent formulations; the robust objective, masking equations and Appendix C lower-bound argument remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims: training-free context-robust revision, benefits under matched computation, and particularly strong code-generation gains, including the same reported 9.2-point MBPP improvement.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 no longer calls the softmax allocation an 'approximate optimal solution', instead describing budget allocation from a margin-based proxy. This modestly qualifies its interpretation; explanations of the results and the limitation concerning factual correctness remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds first-page Project and Code hyperlinks absent from v1, providing new access information. Hardware, precision, hyperparameters and implementation details in Appendix B are unchanged; the PDFs do not establish the linked repository's completeness.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds discussion and citations for Deferred Commitment Decoding, Coherent Contextual Decoding, Information-Gain Sampling and Where-to-Unmask. It extends the positioning of active perturbation-based revision against delayed commitment and learned planners while retaining the existing research framing.

P1.justification: v3 consolidates the context-rigidity discussion in Section 3, expands the masking-distribution and softmax explanations in Section 4, and edits the abstract and qualitative descriptions. The overall section and appendix organization remains intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is revised and relocated, Figure 2 is resized and relocated, and Algorithm 1 moves with the text. Table 5 gains a notation row, while captions, inline code formatting and hyperlink styling receive limited updates; the empirical displays retain their content.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v3 explains the masking formalism more clearly, improves the method schematic, updates relevant research positioning and supplies previously absent project/code access pointers. These modestly improve readability and reproducibility information, while the underlying method, theoretical support and empirical validation remain unchanged.
